name: Amul
summary: Merchants draft and play cards over nine rounds to build tableau and hand sets for prestige points.
rules_text: Amul is played 9 rounds; each round has three phases. Setup: create Palace, Bazaar and a Market deck; deal 5 market cards to each player. Replenish: deal 1 market card to each player, then deal 1-3 cards faceup to the central Market depending on player count. Planning - Offer: each player simultaneously puts one hand card facedown into the Market, then reveal them. Pick: players in order take one faceup Market card to hand; initial order is clockwise from First Pick holder, later ordered by Military Prowess total in play area with tie-break symbols. Reveal: each player simultaneously plays one hand card facedown to personal play area then reveals; cards without play-area icon are discarded, others stay. Upkeep: resolve immediate-effect cards in pick order to gain Palace/Bazaar cards, discard remaining Market cards, pass First Pick clockwise and advance round tracker. After round 9, all remaining hand cards with hand icons move to play area and all tableau cards score by color, Bazaar, and Arab/Mongol symbol majorities. Most prestige wins.
